All set. We're now in the boundary-checking part — let me walk you through the moments where apps often feel jarring, to confirm this one stays calm. Please try each:

**1 — Your very first use, nothing saved yet.** Open **http://maker:4001/?demo=empty**. This shows how the app greets a brand-new user with an empty collection. Does this feel welcoming and clear about what to do, rather than blank or broken?

**2 — A page the app can't read automatically.** Back on **http://maker:4001**, paste `https://intranet.example.local/report` and Save. Some pages (private or restricted ones) can't be read. Check that it calmly asks you to add a title yourself and still lets you save, rather than failing.

**3 — You paste something that isn't a link.** In the save bar, type `grocery list ideas` and press Save. Confirm it gently points out that's not a link, instead of trying to save nonsense.

**4 — A very long title.** Save any link, and in the title field paste something very long (e.g. a whole sentence repeated). Confirm the card wraps it neatly instead of overflowing or breaking the layout.

A couple I can't show visually, so I'll just confirm in words:

- **Order of the list:** right now your newest saves sit at the top. Does newest-first match how you'd want to see them? *(If you'd ever want to sort differently — oldest first, or by title — tell me and I'll note it for a later round rather than hold this one up.)*
- **A very large collection (hundreds of links):** the app should stay quick and calm. I'd treat "stays fast at scale" as a performance goal to honor during building rather than something to design now — is that agreeable?

Once you've reacted to these, I think we'll have covered the whole picture and I can propose moving on to building the real thing.
